runs.text: - Earnings, not debt, are the weak point: reported EBITDA fell USD 99.8 million in FY2025 and its margin fell from 14.11% in FY2023 to 8.35%, so net leverage rose from 3.82x to 6.40x (USD 848.2 million of pro forma net debt after the sale proceeds, with pro forma leverage not established) before the sale improved the balance sheet. Basis: calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C04; calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is the strongest support: cash of USD 397.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418.8 million total USD 815.9 million, which is 1.09x the principal of the 2028 notes, so repaying those notes from liquidity would consume almost all of it and they must be refinanced rather than repaid. Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

- The Feminine Care sale was a good use of an underperforming asset: it was 11.76% of FY2025 net sales but only 5.13% of segment profit and sold for 21.79x that profit, so net debt fell USD 305.0 million at little cost to earnings, although any shared costs it carried are not separated in the filings. Basis: calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C57; calculation C08; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 12

- Wet Shave is the largest segment and the main earnings risk: its segment profit fell USD 31.3 million, or 22.80%, in nine months 2026 and its margin fell from 15.31% to 11.80%, while the unit had only 7% of valuation headroom at the year end. Basis: calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C42; calculation C41; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 78

- Cash generation is thin relative to claims on it: FY2025 free cash flow of USD 41.4 million was 22.31% of reported EBITDA against 61.14% in FY2024, and returns to shareholders of USD 119.5 million exceeded it by USD 78.1 million, so the revolver rose by USD 106.0 million. Basis: calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C30; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

- Covenant reassurance is limited by definitions: the company reported compliance at 2026-06-30, but total debt was 7.61x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 against a 4.0x leverage test, so the covenant EBITDA must carry large add-backs and headroom is not calculable. Basis: calculation C67; calculation C68; calculation C69; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 116; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43

runs.text: - Liquidity and maturity profile is the first strength: USD 815.9 million of cash and undrawn revolver and fixed-rate notes of USD 1,250.0 million due in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 mean no bond falls due before fiscal 2028, which gives time to recover earnings, although the revolver's maturity moves forward to 2028-03-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the 2028 notes remain. Basis: calculation C15; calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 116

- Deleveraging by disposal is the second strength: the Feminine Care sale cut net debt by USD 305.0 million to USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30 and repaid the revolver, which lowers interest expense (USD 16.7 million in the third quarter against USD 19.4 million a year earlier) and restores revolver capacity. Basis: calculation C08; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Brand breadth in Sun and Skin Care is the third strength: the segment grew organic net sales 5.0% in the third quarter, with strong Grooming and North America Sun Care, and earned a segment margin of 14.57% in nine months 2026 against 15.69% a year earlier, so one growing segment partly offsets Wet Shave pressure. Basis: calculation C43; calculation C44; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 14

- Fixed-rate debt is the fourth strength: 97.34% of debt principal is fixed-rate notes, so interest of about USD 70 million in fiscal 2026 does not rise with market rates and only the 2028 refinancing exposes the company to new coupons. Basis: calculation C73; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 46; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Discretionary payouts are the fifth strength because they can be cut: dividends of USD 29.3 million a year and buybacks are choices, and buybacks were USD 15.8 million in nine months 2026 against USD 90.2 million in the same period of FY2025, which shows management can reduce them. Basis: calculation C32; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Falling earnings are the first weakness: reported EBITDA margin fell from 14.11% to 8.35% in two years and nine-month adjusted EBITDA fell 9.66% to USD 177.7 million, so each percentage point of margin that is lost lifts leverage on a fixed debt stack. Basis: calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C37; calculation C38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Wet Shave margin compression is the second weakness: gross margin fell 3.17 percentage points in nine months 2026 as inflation, tariffs, mix and plant consolidation outweighed productivity savings, and Wet Shave profit fell 22.80%. Basis: calculation C48; calculation C40; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Leverage that is high before the sale is the third weakness: net debt was 6.40x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 (USD 848.2 million of net debt pro forma for the sale proceeds on 2026-02-02, with pro forma leverage not established), and the issuer's own adjusted ratio of 3.7x uses a definition that changed each quarter. Basis: calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Payouts above free cash flow in FY2025 are the fourth weakness: returns of USD 119.5 million against free cash flow of USD 41.4 million show that leverage was allowed to rise to fund buybacks, and USD 84.9 million of authorisation remains. Basis: calculation C27; calculation C21; calculation C33; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 44

- Asset quality and concentration are the fifth weakness: goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,940.4 million are 54.88% of assets and exceed equity, one retailer is about 17.4% of net sales, and Wet Shave and the Banana Boat trade name had only 7% and 4% of valuation headroom, so a non-cash impairment or a retailer decision could move equity and covenant add-backs. Basis: calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 78–79; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 5

runs.text: The only transaction in the period is the sale of the Feminine Care business to Essity for USD 340.0 million, agreed on 2025-11-12 and closed on 2026-02-02; the company used the proceeds to repay all revolver borrowings, entered a twelve-month transition services agreement under which Edgewell provides services to Essity, and recorded gross proceeds of USD 338.9 million after a purchase price adjustment of USD 1.1 million. fields.value: This is the financial foundation for EDGEWELL PERSONAL CARE Co as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the audited annual statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025, the interim statements to 2026-06-30, debt at carrying value, liquidity, maturities and the company's non-GAAP measures, with the perimeter change from the Feminine Care sale kept visible.

fields.value: Edgewell's net leverage worsened from 3.82x to 6.40x in FY2025 on lower EBITDA and higher net debt, then net debt fell USD 305.0 million after the Feminine Care sale, but no comparable current leverage exists, so creditors must lean on liquidity.

The company's own adjusted net leverage of 3.7x rests on a definition that changed each quarter, and last-twelve-month continuing EBITDA is missing, so the leverage direction since the sale is not established.

fields.value: This is the business and governance fact pack for EDGEWELL PERSONAL CARE Co as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the company's business model, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation and transaction history from the nine supplied filings and releases, with financial figures taken from the statements only where they explain behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source outside the nine files was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling sponsor is identified in Edgewell's filings, so creditor risk lies in payout policy: FY2025 buybacks and dividends outran free cash flow and were partly debt-funded, while the Feminine Care sale proceeds first repaid the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The retained business is a two-segment personal care group with one retailer at about 17.4% of FY2025 net sales, a restructuring programme of about USD 92 million in fiscal 2026, and a Wet Shave unit whose fair value exceeded its carrying value by only 7% at the year end. Ownership percentages, board committees and the credit documents are not established from the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance looks like that of a widely held listed company rather than a sponsor-controlled one, which removes sponsor extraction as an evidenced risk but does not say who the largest holders are; share buybacks cut shares outstanding by 7.29% in two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payout policy is the governance lever that matters: FY2025 buybacks and dividends of USD 119.5 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 41.4 million and revolver borrowings rose by USD 106.0 million, yet over three years payouts were 82.46% of free cash flow, so the pattern is pressure in one year rather than systematic leakage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Feminine Care sale was used in a creditor-aligned way, because all revolver borrowings were repaid from the proceeds, but a new USD 100.0 million buyback authorisation still has USD 84.9 million unused, so a later switch of liquidity into buybacks remains possible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The retained business is concentrated and under margin pressure: Wet Shave segment profit fell from USD 137.3 million to USD 106.0 million in nine months 2026 and the unit had only 7% valuation headroom at the year end, so a non-cash impairment is a live possibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Seasonal working capital is the liquidity swing: first-quarter operating cash outflow was USD 125.9 million in fiscal 2026 and revolver borrowings reached USD 277.0 million before the sale proceeds repaid them, so the USD 425.0 million revolver is the seasonal funding source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Finance leadership changed in 2024 and the chief operating officer left in 2025, but the audit opinion is unqualified and internal control over reporting is effective, so continuity risk is a monitoring point and not an adverse finding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a payout-pressure reading is that payouts were 82.46% of three-year free cash flow, dividends stayed at USD 0.15 per share each quarter, nine-month 2026 buybacks were only USD 15.8 million, and the sale proceeds went to repay the revolver first. The view would turn more adverse if buybacks again exceed free cash flow after the revolver is redrawn, if a holder above 5% with control rights is disclosed, or if the credit agreement shows wide restricted-payment capacity; it would turn more favourable if the unused authorisation lapses and the retained business returns to organic growth, as it did in the third quarter with growth of 1.1%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the absence of a named sponsor and would change if a holder above 5% or any control right is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only transaction in the period is the sale of the Feminine Care business to Essity for USD 340.0 million, agreed on 2025-11-12 and closed on 2026-02-02; the company used the proceeds to repay all revolver borrowings, entered a twelve-month transition services agreement under which Edgewell provides services to Essity, and recorded gross proceeds of USD 338.9 million after a purchase price adjustment of USD 1.1 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company issued no new notes in the period read: the two fixed-rate note series of USD 750.0 million and USD 500.0 million are unchanged from 2024-09-30 to 2026-06-30, and the only debt event is the April 2, 2024 amendment and restatement that extended the USD 425.0 million revolver to April 2, 2029 with earlier springing dates tied to the two note series. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This analysis covers EDGEWELL PERSONAL CARE Co as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the company's fundamental credit profile from the nine supplied filings and releases and from the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source outside the nine files and the three supplied analyses was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Edgewell's liquidity of USD 815.9 million and the absence of bond maturities before fiscal 2028 protect creditors for now, but weaker earnings leave refinancing of the 2028 notes dependent on a recovery that the nine-month results do not yet show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 1,187.1 million at 2025-09-30, or 6.40x reported EBITDA of USD 185.6 million, and USD 848.2 million pro forma for the sale proceeds received on 2026-02-02; pro forma net leverage is not established. Net debt was USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30, but no earnings base for the retained business supports a current ratio, so the judgement rests on liquidity, a fixed-rate debt stack and management's outlook of adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C06; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings, not debt, are the weak point: reported EBITDA fell USD 99.8 million in FY2025 and its margin fell from 14.11% in FY2023 to 8.35%, so net leverage rose from 3.82x to 6.40x (USD 848.2 million of pro forma net debt after the sale proceeds, with pro forma leverage not established) before the sale improved the balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C04; calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is the strongest support: cash of USD 397.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418.8 million total USD 815.9 million, which is 1.09x the principal of the 2028 notes, so repaying those notes from liquidity would consume almost all of it and they must be refinanced rather than repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Feminine Care sale was a good use of an underperforming asset: it was 11.76% of FY2025 net sales but only 5.13% of segment profit and sold for 21.79x that profit, so net debt fell USD 305.0 million at little cost to earnings, although any shared costs it carried are not separated in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C57; calculation C08; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Wet Shave is the largest segment and the main earnings risk: its segment profit fell USD 31.3 million, or 22.80%, in nine months 2026 and its margin fell from 15.31% to 11.80%, while the unit had only 7% of valuation headroom at the year end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C42; calculation C41; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 78

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation is thin relative to claims on it: FY2025 free cash flow of USD 41.4 million was 22.31% of reported EBITDA against 61.14% in FY2024, and returns to shareholders of USD 119.5 million exceeded it by USD 78.1 million, so the revolver rose by USD 106.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C30; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant reassurance is limited by definitions: the company reported compliance at 2026-06-30, but total debt was 7.61x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 against a 4.0x leverage test, so the covenant EBITDA must carry large add-backs and headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C67; calculation C68; calculation C69; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 66, 116; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the retained business has stabilised: third-quarter organic net sales grew 1.1% with North America up 3.0%, Sun and Skin Care organic net sales grew 5.0%, interest expense fell to USD 16.7 million in the quarter, and management guides to adjusted EBITDA of USD 250 million to USD 260 million, which implies USD 72.3 million to USD 82.3 million in the fourth quarter against USD 78.9 million in the third. The view would turn favourable if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA lands inside that range, Wet Shave profit stops falling and the 2028 notes are reduced or refinanced before 2028-03-02. It would turn adverse if adjusted EBITDA falls below USD 250 million, if buybacks resume ahead of free cash flow, or if the next annual report shows covenant headroom narrower than the add-backs suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C58; calculation C59; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5, 14; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 66

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Net leverage and interest cover for the retained business after the sale cannot be computed from the supplied statements, so the improvement from FY2025 is shown by net debt and liquidity and would be overturned if trailing earnings of the two continuing segments prove well below the outlook.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, bond price, peer leverage or sector spread is supplied, so the judgement that the business profile is average and refinancing capacity adequate rests on the maturity profile and liquidity and not on a market comparison, and a weak refinancing market for consumer credits would lower it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth-quarter outlook is management's own and was issued on 2026-08-05, so the view that earnings recover in the last quarter of fiscal 2026 is untested and would change with the first results published after that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions are described but not tested because compliance certificates are not supplied, so the conclusion that near-term default risk is low rests on reported compliance plus liquidity and would weaken if the definitions allow smaller add-backs than the figures imply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fixed overhead that was shared with Feminine Care is not separated in any source, so the conclusion that the sale cost little earnings would weaken if stranded costs prove large.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and maturity profile is the first strength: USD 815.9 million of cash and undrawn revolver and fixed-rate notes of USD 1,250.0 million due in fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 mean no bond falls due before fiscal 2028, which gives time to recover earnings, although the revolver's maturity moves forward to 2028-03-02 if more than USD 150.0 million of the 2028 notes remain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C72; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 43, 46; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 116

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Deleveraging by disposal is the second strength: the Feminine Care sale cut net debt by USD 305.0 million to USD 882.1 million at 2026-06-30 and repaid the revolver, which lowers interest expense (USD 16.7 million in the third quarter against USD 19.4 million a year earlier) and restores revolver capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C08; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 43; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Brand breadth in Sun and Skin Care is the third strength: the segment grew organic net sales 5.0% in the third quarter, with strong Grooming and North America Sun Care, and earned a segment margin of 14.57% in nine months 2026 against 15.69% a year earlier, so one growing segment partly offsets Wet Shave pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C43; calculation C44; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fixed-rate debt is the fourth strength: 97.34% of debt principal is fixed-rate notes, so interest of about USD 70 million in fiscal 2026 does not rise with market rates and only the 2028 refinancing exposes the company to new coupons.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Discretionary payouts are the fifth strength because they can be cut: dividends of USD 29.3 million a year and buybacks are choices, and buybacks were USD 15.8 million in nine months 2026 against USD 90.2 million in the same period of FY2025, which shows management can reduce them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Falling earnings are the first weakness: reported EBITDA margin fell from 14.11% to 8.35% in two years and nine-month adjusted EBITDA fell 9.66% to USD 177.7 million, so each percentage point of margin that is lost lifts leverage on a fixed debt stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C12; calculation C37; calculation C38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Wet Shave margin compression is the second weakness: gross margin fell 3.17 percentage points in nine months 2026 as inflation, tariffs, mix and plant consolidation outweighed productivity savings, and Wet Shave profit fell 22.80%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C48; calculation C40; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage that is high before the sale is the third weakness: net debt was 6.40x reported EBITDA at 2025-09-30 (USD 848.2 million of net debt pro forma for the sale proceeds on 2026-02-02, with pro forma leverage not established), and the issuer's own adjusted ratio of 3.7x uses a definition that changed each quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payouts above free cash flow in FY2025 are the fourth weakness: returns of USD 119.5 million against free cash flow of USD 41.4 million show that leverage was allowed to rise to fund buybacks, and USD 84.9 million of authorisation remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C27; calculation C21; calculation C33; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Asset quality and concentration are the fifth weakness: goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,940.4 million are 54.88% of assets and exceed equity, one retailer is about 17.4% of net sales, and Wet Shave and the Banana Boat trade name had only 7% and 4% of valuation headroom, so a non-cash impairment or a retailer decision could move equity and covenant add-backs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C64; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 78–79; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Edgewell is a branded and private-label personal care manufacturer with two continuing segments, Wet Shave and Sun and Skin Care, sold mainly through mass merchants, food, drug and convenience retailers and online. Revenue is spread across razors and blades, sun care and grooming and skin care products rather than one product, which supports cash-flow visibility, but one retailer accounts for about 17.4% of net sales and orders are shipped within a month, so there is no contracted backlog to support debt service in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is seasonal: sun care sells from late winter to mid-summer, so the first quarter consumes cash (operating cash outflow of USD 125.9 million against USD 115.6 million a year earlier, consolidated) and the revolver was drawn to USD 277.0 million at 2025-12-31 before the sale. Cash plus revolver availability fell USD 139.4 million in that quarter to USD 365.8 million, before the sale proceeds, so the seasonal cycle can consume a large part of the USD 815.9 million shown at 2026-06-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C17; calculation C20; calculation C77; calculation C15; EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_epcexhibit99112312025-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so decisions on payouts and disposals rest with the board, and the record is mixed: shares outstanding fell 7.29% in two years through buybacks, FY2025 returns exceeded free cash flow, but the proceeds of the Feminine Care sale first repaid the revolver. Ownership percentages and the credit documents are not supplied, so legal capacity to make further payouts is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C75; calculation C27; calculation C21; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is stable rather than growing: net sales were USD 2,251.6 million, USD 2,253.7 million and USD 2,223.5 million in FY2023 to FY2025, and organic net sales fell 1.3% in FY2025 on lower North America volumes in Wet Shave, Feminine Care and Sun Care. In fiscal 2026 so far organic growth was negative in the first two quarters (0.5% and 2.4% declines) and positive 1.1% in the third, so durability depends on the third-quarter recovery in North America holding and on Wet Shave supply constraints easing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, pages 58, 89; EX99.1_2025-12-31_epc_epcexhibit99112312025-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-03-31_epc_epcexhibit99103312026-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are the weakest dimension: FY2025 gross margin was 41.60% against 42.41%, adjusted gross margin fell 110 bp (20 bp excluding currency) as productivity savings of 270 bp were outweighed by 150 bp of core inflation including tariffs, 75 bp of mix, 45 bp of promotions and 20 bp of absorption, and in nine months 2026 gross margin fell 3.17 percentage points to 41.02%. Advertising and overhead rose at the same time (advertising and promotion 14.59% of third-quarter net sales against 13.56%), so operating leverage is working against the company while volumes are flat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C49; calculation C50; calculation C51; calculation C47; calculation C46; calculation C48; calculation C52; calculation C53; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 58; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA of USD 97.4 million in nine months 2026 against USD 158.0 million a year earlier (a fall of USD 60.6 million) is on the continuing perimeter, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 177.7 million includes add-backs equal to 45.19% of itself and transition services income that lasts twelve months, which was 9.76% of third-quarter adjusted EBITDA. Run-rate earnings are therefore weaker than the adjusted figure alone suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C54; calculation C65; calculation C66; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16–17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditures are moderate at USD 77.0 million in FY2025 (3.46% of net sales) and are guided to 3.0% to 3.5% of net sales in fiscal 2026, but cash conversion has weakened: free cash flow was USD 166.6 million, USD 174.5 million and USD 41.4 million in FY2023 to FY2025, or 52.46%, 61.14% and 22.31% of reported EBITDA, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow on a consolidated basis was USD 5.9 million. A split between maintenance and growth capital is not stated, so flexibility to cut capital spending cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C36; calculation C23; calculation C22; calculation C21; calculation C26; calculation C25; calculation C24; calculation C31; 10-K_2025-09-30_epc.htm.jsonl, page 91; EX99.1_2026-06-30_epc_q3fy26-epcexhibit991-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Restructuring and tax cash costs sit ahead of free cash flow: about USD 92 million of pre-tax restructuring charges are expected in fiscal 2026 with USD 71.9 million incurred in nine months (about USD 20.1 million to come), and about USD 55 million of cash taxes on the gain from the sale is expected in the same year. Management guides adjusted free cash flow of USD 80 million to USD 110 million, which excludes divestiture cash effects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense in Wet Shave, where The Procter & Gamble Company leads, BIC is expanding and Dorco competes in private label, and online and direct-to-consumer start-ups compete for shelf space; this explains the 7.2% fall in North America Wet Shave organic sales in FY2025 and caps pricing, so margin recovery depends on productivity rather than price. Substitutes and new entrants matter mainly through private label and direct brands, which is why lower private label sales from supply constraints in the third quarter hurt Wet Shave.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is the largest structural force: one retailer is about 17.4% of net sales and a few retailers account for a large share, so shelf-space or terms changes pass quickly into volume and margin. Supplier power is moderate because the principal inputs of steel, plastic resins, fabrics and chemicals are mostly available from several sources, but tariffs and inflation cost 160 bp of gross margin in the third quarter, which shows inputs still move earnings.

Sun Care is a regulated category and reformulation, recall and destruction costs of USD 3.4 million were incurred in nine months 2026, and the Middle East conflict disrupted international sales in the third quarter; currency was a small favourable factor in the third quarter, so it is not a primary driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a Wet Shave supply disruption that lasts longer than management expects: plant consolidation continues to constrain private label and international supply, a retailer reallocates shelf space to a competitor, and tariff costs remain. The first operational break is lost Wet Shave volume in North America, where organic sales already fell 7.2% in FY2025, with promotions rising to defend share. Financially, Wet Shave profit, which already fell USD 31.3 million in nine months, falls further and adjusted EBITDA lands below USD 250 million, so net leverage rises on an unchanged debt stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity absorbs the shock before leverage forces a decision: the first-quarter seasonal outflow, about USD 20.1 million of remaining restructuring costs and the cash taxes on the gain draw on cash, and a revolver that is used in the seasonal trough narrows the cushion for the 2028 notes. Management levers are to stop buybacks, cut capital expenditures and phase the remaining restructuring spend, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before the 2028 notes fall due, on the liquidity shown at 2026-06-30, but a covenant test measured on a weaker EBITDA is the observable trigger because its headroom is not calculable. The primary downside path is a Wet Shave earnings decline that leaves the company refinancing the 2028 notes at higher leverage.

fields.value: Overall, Edgewell presents a not fully assessable business profile that is average on scale and diversification, supported by liquidity of USD 815.9 million and a fixed-rate debt stack with no maturity before fiscal 2028, but credit quality is constrained by a reported EBITDA margin of 8.35% in FY2025, Wet Shave margin compression and payouts that exceeded free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was 22.31% of reported EBITDA in FY2025, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Wet Shave earnings, liquidity at the seasonal trough and the springing maturity date of 2028-03-02. The primary downside path is Wet Shave earnings falling while the 2028 notes approach maturity. Further analysis would require trailing continuing-operations EBITDA, covenant calculations and peer data. Top risk: Wet Shave earnings decline before the 2028 refinancing.
